findings.issue: At ≥1024px the Pletenice section's braid arch collapses to a 110px-wide, 416px-tall pointed sliver instead of the intended 20rem-wide door. `lg:ml-auto` on the wrapper cancels the grid item's justify-self:stretch, so the item becomes fit-content and shrink-wraps the SVG's intrinsic width=96; `lg:max-w-[20rem]` never binds. The result reads as a surfboard/zipper strip, has a pinched ogive dome unlike every other arch on the page, and leaves the whole section roughly 85% empty (a ~240px void under the left column beside a 110px visual). Fix: replace `lg:ml-auto lg:mr-0` with `lg:justify-self-end` (or add `lg:w-full`) so stretch survives and max-w-[20rem] applies.

overall: Eight of eleven plan changes are genuinely on the page and several are done well — the closing-grid blocker, the tablet CTA wrap, the per-room DOOR_LAYOUT hallway, the arch mat/box/photo split, the one-knock motion budget with kraftart's drawn hover rule, and the honest above-fold kicker all survive pixel scrutiny, and the keep-list is intact (FloatingDoor byte-identical, researchOnly untouched, the plait's over/under z-order and the arch motif preserved, no forbidden data rendered). But the fixer's own warning was right: the layout was verified by arithmetic, not rendering, and the single most important change failed in the browser — the Pletenice arch collapses to a 110px sliver at desktop because an auto margin kills grid stretch, which leaves the page's one drawn signature at a third of its intended width and the section around it 85% empty. Add the still-flat braid terminals, the interpuncts that merely moved from the right margin to the left, and the 64px rail break on the newly-promoted peak section, and the page is not yet at the level of the best four demos. None of the four is expensive: three are one-line class or path changes.

Braids arch collapsed to a 110px sliver at lg (page.tsx, #pletenice) → FIXED. Verified by raw-pixel scan of andrea-beauty-house-desktop.png: the berry field measures x=1146..1255 (110px wide) against a 416px height — ratio 0.26, a surfboard, where `lg:max-w-[20rem]` intended a 304px box at ratio 0.73 to match the salon and enterijer arches. Root cause: the container carried base `mx-auto` plus `lg:ml-auto lg:mr-0`, and an auto margin on a grid item switches off the default `justify-self: stretch`, so the item shrank to fit-content — which for this door is the Braid SVG's own natural width (h-[86%] of 416px = 358px tall x 96/312 ratio = 110px) plus 16px of mat padding. Every other arch on the page escapes this because its fit-content comes from a photograph. Fix, in the existing house style (the salon figure already uses this idiom): the container is now `lg:mx-0 lg:max-w-none` so it stretches, and the grid track is sized explicitly as `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_20rem]` instead of `[1.25fr_0.75fr]` so the door fills a deliberate 320px column flush to the container edge rather than relying on an auto-margin trick. Left track becomes 728px; the heading still sets on one line. Two short comments added explaining why the track is in rem and why `lg:mx-0` is load-bearing. Keep-list respected: the plait, its over/under z-order, repeat count, weight and the archMat/archBox split are untouched — only the box it stands in was un-collapsed.
